{{Quote|Perhaps you are familiar with my executioner, Lomrokk. Renowned for his killing prowess in fighting pits across the Outer Rim.|Jabba Desilijic Tiure, to Longo Two-Guns|<ref name="mythos" />}}
'''Lomrokk''' was a [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] [[Warlord (Gamorrean)/Legends|warlord]] and later executioner for [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lord]] [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]]. Lomrokk became famous across the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] for his talent for [[Death/Legends|killing]] in [[pit fighting]] matches. This reputation secured him a position as Jabba's [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiator]] and personal executioner before the introduction of the [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|rancor]] creature in [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]. According to most, the Gamorrean was responsible for the death of notorious [[Clantaani]] criminal [[Longo Two-Guns]].

==Biography==
{{Quote|The blade he wields has ended the life of every creature he has met in combat. With it, Lomrokk has even slain a mighty gundark.|Jabba Desilijic Tiure|<ref name="mythos" />}}
[[File:Lomrokk_art.png|thumb|left|300px|Lomrokk served as Jabba the Hutt's personal gladiator and main executioner.]]
A former [[Warlord (Gamorrean)/Legends|warlord]], the [[Gamorrean/Legends|Gamorrean]] Lomrokk at one point was deposed of his position and turned to [[pit fighting]], which earned him a reputation across the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] for his [[Death/Legends|killing]] prowess. His reputation was heightened after he slew a [[Gundark/Legends|gundark]],<ref name="mythos" /> a large and [[Sentience/Legends|semi-sentient]] four-[[Limb/Legends|armed]] [[Humanoid/Legends|anthropoid]] known for its incredible strength.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|374|gundark}}</ref> The Gamorrean was then hired by [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]],<ref name="mythos" /> one of the most notorious [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] [[Crime lord/Legends|crime lords]] in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="TEGTC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref> Lomrokk joined [[Jabba's criminal empire/Legends|Jabba's criminal empire]] as the Hutt's personal [[Gladiator/Legends|gladiator]] and main executioner at the [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Hutt Castle]],<ref name="mythos" /> which was located in the [[Northern Dune Sea/Legends|Northern Dune Sea]] of the [[Desert/Legends|desert]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="IWSW">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref> The former warlord's employment in Jabba's castle occurred before the introduction of the [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|rancor]],<ref name="mythos" /> a large [[Dathomir/Legends|Dathomiri]] [[Reptomammal/Legends|reptomammal]] that the Hutt used to dispose of his enemies,<ref name="SWCE">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> which took place between [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] and [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="tale">''[[A Boy and His Monster: The Rancor Keeper's Tale]]'' depicts the introduction of the [[Jabba's rancor/Legends|rancor]] to [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]]. ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''A Boy and His Monster'' between [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]] and [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].</ref>

In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],<ref name="TNEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Jabba placed a 50,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credit]] [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] on the head of [[Clantaani]] criminal [[Longo Two-Guns]], known to some as the "fastest [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] on Tatooine." [[Bounty hunter/Legends|Bounty hunter]] [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] then captured Longo and brought him to the Hutt.<ref name="SWBH">''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]''</ref> After that, the most accepted version of his death<ref name="blog">{{SW|url=news/so-uncivilized-great-gunslingers-in-star-wars-part-1|series=So Uncivilized: Great Gunslingers in Star Wars|text=Part 1|nolive=1}}</ref> was that Jabba then threw Longo down the shaft that led to the fighting pit, where Lomrokk was expected to execute the [[Gangster/Legends|gangster]]. The Gamorrean initially punched Longo Two-Guns, sending him flying across the pit, and then, under Jabba's command, Lomrokk [[Axe/Legends|axed]] and killed the Clantaani.<ref name="mythos" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|So tell me, bounty hunter. Unarmed and unarmored, how do you think you will fare against the likes of Lomrokk?|Jabba Desilijic Tiure, to Longo Two-Guns|<ref name="mythos" />}}
Lomrokk was a ruthless,<ref name="statue">{{SideshowCite|set=Star Wars Mythos|text=''Star Wars Mythos''|pack=Gamorrean Executioner|link=collectibles/star-wars-gamorrean-executioner-mythos-sideshow-collectibles-200154}}</ref> [[Color/Legends|dark-green]]-skinned Gamorrean, more physically imposing and intelligent than most members of his [[Species/Legends|species]]. He also stood two heads taller<ref name="mythos" /> than the Gamorrean average of 1.8 [[Meter/Legends|meters]]<ref name="NEGAS" /> and bore many battle scars, gashed across his fat and muscled body. Lomrokk was made famous in the Outer Rim for his killing skills, exterminating every creature he had met in combat. Longo Two-Guns, one of his victims, noticed a particularly cruel intellect behind Lomrokk's [[Eye/Legends|eyes]], something that Longo had never seen before.<ref name="mythos" />

==Equipment==
Lomrokk wielded a giant [[Gamorrean war ax/Legends|battleaxe]]. He worked topless, wearing [[Hair/Legends|furred]] shorts and a [[Belt/Legends|belt]], as well as shoulder pads and [[Bracelet/Legends|bracelets]].<ref name="mythos" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|This figure represents a true test of our Mythos theme as we set out to shape our first original addition to the Star Wars universe.|''Star Wars Mythos'' team|<ref name="mythos" />}}
[[File:SWMythos_Lomrokk_CONCEPT1.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Concept art for Lomrokk, depicting a tauntaun skull at the base]]
Lomrokk was created for a short story as Longo Two-Guns's executioner in the [[Canon|non-canon]]<ref name="Canon">According to the {{WebCite|url=http://www.sideshowtoy.com/experience/entertainment/main-attractions/star-wars-page/star-wars-mythos|text=Star Wars Mythos website|work=[https://www.sideshow.com/ Sideshow]|archivedate=20150117164147|nolive=1}}, ''[[Star Wars Mythos]]'' aims to "offer [its] own interpretations of what [the characters] have done outside of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]]."</ref> [[2012]] ''[[Star Wars Mythos]]'' project, an initiative of [[Sideshow Collectibles]]. The narrative was published online on Sideshow's website. ''Star Wars Mythos'' further elaborates on the story of Longo Two-Guns,<ref name="mythos" /> which originated with the [[2002]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Bounty Hunter]]'',<ref name="SWBH" /> while also introducing the Gamorrean character Lomrokk.<ref name="mythos" /> The project also included the production of a nineteen-inch-tall polystone statue of the executioner, the third in a series of five characters that were commissioned.<ref name="mythos" /><ref name="statue" />

The general style and aesthetics of Lomrokk's illustration were inspired by forms often seen in the barbarian paintings of science-fiction artist [[Wikipedia:Frank Frazetta|Frank Frazetta]]. The [[Tauntaun/Legends|tauntaun]] [[Bone/Legends|skull]], featured in the concept art sketches and the final statue model, was added in order to allude to the [[Wikipedia:Colosseum|Colosseum]] in [[Wikipedia:Italy|Italy]] and its gladiatorial fights in [[Wikipedia:Ancient Rome|Ancient Rome]]. Involved in the making of Lomrokk were artists [[Tom Gilliland]] and [[Seth Rinaldi]], designer [[David Igo]], sculptor [[Michael Norman]], and painters [[Anthony Mestas]], [[Steve Riojas]], [[Jesse Lincoln]], and [[Ian MacDonald]].<ref name="mythos" /><ref name="statue" />

Lomrokk was mentioned again in the first part of [[Star Wars Blog|The Official ''Star Wars'' Blog]] series "[[So Uncivilized: Great Gunslingers in Star Wars]]," written by [[Edward M. Erdelac|Ed Erdelac]] and released on [[September 19]], [[2013]]. This article therefore treats the ''Mythos'' details as [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] canon.<ref name="blog" />
